correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the exact pointwise deductions from Fletcher 2026 Theorem 1.2 for every n>=2 and every uniformly quasiregular f:B^n->B^n. The theorem asserts exactly (a) every orbit relatively compact, split into locally uniform f^m->x0 with unique attracting/superattracting fixed point or onto uniformly quasiconformal d-isometric homeomorphism with subsequential identity; (b) all f^m->w in the boundary. A prime q>=2 periodic x gives finite compact orbit and excludes (b); the nonconstant periodic sequence f^m(x) has no limit, excluding the attracting branch, hence forces the homeomorphism branch. Outside that branch, in (a) all f^m(x)->x0 so a periodic or recurrent x is x0, and x0 itself is fixed/recurrent; in (b), every interior orbit tends to w on the sphere, excluding relatively compact, periodic, or recurrent interior points. Thus fixed/periodic/recurrent/some compact orbit exist together in (a), and none in (b). The q=1 case, q>=2 case, n=2 case, and boundary escape are consistent. The proof uses only exact convergence/compactness and no numerical computation or unchecked certificate. This C PASS is conditional on the cited deep source theorem, independently read but not reproved.

originality.rationale: All parts of the submitted final claim are immediate implications of Fletcher's Theorem 1.2 (2026), the very result cited as the proof's sole premise. Naming a new orbit-level corollary, or observing that the lead paper does not contain the words 'recurrent' or 'periodic point', cannot defeat implication-level coverage. For a prime q>=2 cycle the finite orbit rules out boundary escape, while its nonconvergent time sequence excludes convergence to x0, leaving exactly the isometric homeomorphism branch of that theorem. In the excluded-elliptic regime the same dichotomy already determines periodic and recurrent sets by taking limits. Resultary's match is this same assessed record, never independent priority. This is a scientifically decisive O failure, not an access or failed-search shortcut.

value.rationale: Periodic and recurrent orbit sets are natural dynamical objects, and the stated diagnostic is educationally useful. Nonetheless the entire classification is obtained by taking constant limits of a sequence and ruling out convergence of a nonconstant periodic sequence. It introduces no new geometric estimate, structural lemma, boundary example, quantitative restriction, classification not already implicit in the complete source trichotomy, or independent invariant calculation. The gain over Fletcher 2026 Theorem 1.2 is terminology/exposition, precisely the kind of routine corollary the standard excludes as a stand-alone research contribution. The basic orbit-logic is not a motivated additional mathematical gap requiring a research finding.
residual_risks: An expository corollary could help readers locate periodic behavior, but usefulness in exposition is not by itself substantive standalone scientific value.

limitations: The result is conditional on the deep 2026 preprint theorem, which is cited rather than reproved.
No generalization to globally defined maps or dynamics in the isometric homeomorphism branch.
